Dear Dr. Miller,

Thank you for evaluating Julian, a 7-year-old boy I have followed since early childhood. His parents bring him for your assessment regarding several congenital orthopedic and dermatologic anomalies.

Julian had reduced muscular tone evident since birth, and he continues to exhibit generalized muscular flaccidity on examination alongside marked articular laxity, with joint hyperextensibility evident across both his upper and lower extremities. Palpation of the anterior knees reveals a complete absence of kneecaps, and bilateral knee films confirmed total agenesis of the patellae. He also displays dystrophic, poorly formed nails characterized by severe longitudinal ridging, split free edges, and hypoplasia, predominantly affecting the thumbs and index fingers. In addition, a pelvic radiograph obtained to evaluate his mechanics demonstrated prominent, symmetric bony spurs projecting from the posterior aspects of the iliac bones. 

Of note, repeated spot urinalyses have been entirely negative for protein, and his serum creatinine was completely normal. Julian is otherwise thriving in the second grade, enjoys swimming, and takes only a daily chewable multivitamin. His vital signs, height, and weight are tracking along the 50th percentile. Cardiac auscultation, respiratory effort, and a recent visual screening were all unremarkable. His family history is non-contributory, with both parents and his older sister in good health.

I would be most grateful for your clinical assessment and any recommendations for his ongoing surveillance.

Sincerely,

Dr. Marcus Vance, MD
Pediatric Primary Care
